slides.title: You met Islam only through anger?
slides.promise: The truth doesn't reach everyone in the same shape. Only God sees the whole road.

slides.head: A face we see. A heart we don't.
slides.body: Every person has a face others can see, and a heart only God knows completely. Their intentions, struggles and questions stay out of our sight.

slides.head: We see one moment
slides.body: God sees the whole road: what reached a person and what didn't, what was grasped and what was misread.

slides.quote: How, then, can someone who has read only one page pass judgement upon an entire book?

slides.head: Deal with what you see
slides.body: This is why Islam rests our dealings with people on what they visibly do, and leaves the final judgement of belief and intention to God.

slides.head: Nobody starts from the same place
slides.body: Not the same family, culture or circumstances. One reads the Qur'an in a language he understands. Another is handed fragments and poor translations.

slides.head: Mercy for one, anger for another
slides.body: One person meets Islam through a Muslim whose honesty and mercy show its beauty. Another meets it only through anger, injustice or disturbing images.

slides.head: How much light? How much smoke?
slides.body: We can't tell how much light reached someone, or how much smoke stood in its way. Someone far from faith may be searching quietly.

slides.head: Before you judge a heart
items: We see a face. God knows the heart.
We see one moment. God sees the whole road.
Deal with what people visibly do.
Truth doesn't reach everyone in the same shape.
Someone counted as lost may be moving towards the truth.

slides.head: Read the full reflection
slides.ask: Send this to someone who has ever been judged from one page.
